ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: According to the schematic diagram in Figure 7 showing air pressure changes when different weather systems pass through a certain place, which curve produces the midsummer drought weather in the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River? <image1>
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the horizontal axis is time (days), from 1 to 5; the vertical direction represents air pressure changes. There are four curves ①②③④ in the figure: ① rises in the later period and maintains relatively high air pressure; ②, before and after the weather system passes, shows a rise first, reaches a peak around the 3rd day, and then falls back to close to the original level; ③ decreases first and then rises back; ④ gradually decreases and then maintains a low value. Then reason: the midsummer drought in the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River is mainly formed under the control of the subtropical high. When the center of a high-pressure system passes through a certain place, the air pressure there should first rise, reach a high value when the center passes, and then decrease and recover afterward. The one in the figure that conforms to this change characteristic is curve ②, so the answer is 2.

根据图7所示不同天气系统经过某地时的气压变化示意图，产生长江中下游地区伏旱天气的是哪条曲线？

There are four curves ①②③④ in the figure: ① rises in the later period and maintains relatively high air pressure; ②, before and after the weather system passes, shows a rise first, reaches a peak around the 3rd day, and then falls back to close to the original level; ③ decreases first and then rises back; ④ gradually decreases and then maintains a low value. Then reason: the midsummer drought in the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River is mainly formed under the control of the subtropical high. When the center of a high-pressure system passes through a certain place, the air pressure there should first rise, reach a high value when the center passes, and then decrease and recover afterward. The one in the figure that conforms to this change characteristic is curve ②, so the answer is 2.
